outputs.L1: The present invention relates to a test system for multi-fuel, high-temperature fuel cells that enables the direct use of carbon-based fuels, including anhydrous fuels, without promoting or limiting carbon deposition in the gas inlet and outlet ducts or in the anode flow channels. The system comprises a furnace (5) containing a reactor (4), the reactor comprising at least two interconnection plates and at least one fuel cell (15) positioned between two interconnection plates. One of the interconnection plates in contact with the fuel cell forms a cathodic side that receives an oxidizing gas, while the other interconnection plate in contact with the fuel cell forms an anodic side that receives a combustible gas. The system further comprises controlled gas supply and exhaust means connected to the reactor (4). Each plate further comprises a plurality of flow channels (14) on its upper and lower surfaces, through which the oxidizing gas and the combustible gas pass to contact the electrodes of the fuel cell (15). The base, top, and interconnection plates are made of a zirconium oxide- or cerium oxide-based material doped with one or more oxides selected from yttria, scandia, calcia, gadolinia, samaria, alumina, and cobaltite, with the total amount of dopants being up to 20% by weight.
outputs.L2: The invention concerns a testing apparatus for high-temperature, multi-fuel fuel cells that can operate directly with carbon-based fuels, including water-free fuels, without encouraging or restricting carbon buildup in the gas inlet and outlet conduits or in the anode flow channels. The apparatus includes a furnace (5) housing a reactor (4). The reactor has at least two interconnection plates and at least one fuel cell (15) positioned between a pair of those plates. Of the plates adjoining the fuel cell, one forms the cathode side and is supplied with an oxidizing gas, while the other forms the anode side and receives a combustible gas. A regulated gas-supply and exhaust arrangement is also connected to the reactor (4). Each plate has multiple flow channels (14) on both its upper and lower surfaces. The oxidizing and combustible gases travel through these channels (14) and come into contact with the fuel-cell electrodes. The base, top, and interconnection plates are manufactured from a zirconium-oxide- or cerium-oxide-based material doped with one or more oxides selected from yttria, scandia, calcia, gadolinia, samaria, alumina, and cobaltite, with the combined dopant content not exceeding 20% by weight.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a test system for multi-fuel, high-temperature fuel cells capable of directly utilizing carbon-based fuels, including anhydrous fuels. The system is designed to operate without actively promoting or suppressing carbon deposition within the gas inlet and outlet ducts or within the anode flow channels, thereby enabling testing under conditions representative of direct fuel use.

The system includes a furnace containing a reactor. The reactor comprises at least two interconnection plates and at least one fuel cell arranged between the plates. During operation, the cathodic side of the fuel cell receives an oxidizing gas, while the anodic side receives a combustible gas. These gases are supplied and removed through a controlled gas-feeding and exhaust system in fluid communication with corresponding flow channels formed in the interconnection plates.

The reactor further includes base, top, and interconnection plates made from materials based on doped zirconium oxide or doped cerium oxide. The total concentration of dopants in these materials is limited to no more than 20% by weight. This configuration provides a controlled platform for evaluating the performance and behavior of high-temperature fuel cells with different fuels and under varied operating conditions.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a test system for multifuel, high-temperature fuel cells, particularly fuel cells capable of operating directly with carbon-containing fuels. The system is suitable for evaluating conventional gaseous fuels as well as substantially anhydrous fuels, thereby permitting fuel-cell performance to be studied under a broad range of operating conditions.

The test system includes a reactor located within a temperature-controlled furnace. One or more fuel cells are arranged in the reactor together with interconnection plates formed from, or containing, doped zirconia- or doped ceria-based ceramic materials. The interconnection plates provide electrical connection between adjacent cells and include flow channels that distribute gases over the corresponding electrode surfaces. Their ceramic composition and configuration are selected to withstand the elevated operating temperatures and the oxidizing and reducing environments encountered during testing.

Separate gas-feeding arrangements supply an oxidizing gas to the cathode side and a combustible gas or fuel mixture to the anode side. Associated control devices regulate parameters such as gas composition, flow rate, pressure, and, where appropriate, temperature. Exhaust conduits remove reaction products and unused gases from the reactor while maintaining separation between the oxidizing and fuel streams. This arrangement allows the respective gases to contact the electrodes in a controlled and reproducible manner.

The fuel-delivery path, reactor configuration, and anode-side flow channels are designed to avoid or substantially limit carbon deposition. In particular, the system reduces the likelihood that carbon will accumulate in supply ducts or obstruct the anode channels when carbon-based or low-moisture fuels are used. Appropriate thermal management, gas-flow control, material selection, and channel geometry may be employed to keep the fuel in a condition suitable for delivery to the electrochemically active region and to suppress premature cracking or coking.

During operation, the furnace brings the reactor and fuel-cell assembly to the required high temperature. The controlled gas-feeding system then delivers oxidant and fuel to the cathode and anode, respectively. Electrochemical measurements can be made while varying the fuel composition and operating conditions, allowing the electrical output, efficiency, stability, durability, and resistance to carbon formation to be assessed.

By enabling direct testing with a wider variety of carbon-based fuels, including anhydrous or substantially anhydrous fuels, the invention provides a reliable and versatile platform for the development and characterization of multifuel, high-temperature fuel cells. The reduced risk of carbon blockage or contamination improves test continuity, measurement repeatability, and the useful operating life of the reactor and fuel-cell components.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “the book” refers to a particular book rather than any book.

Although it consists of only three letters, “the” plays an essential role in clear communication. It helps add context, directs attention, and shows that the speaker and listener understand what is being discussed. This small word demonstrates how even the simplest parts of language can have a significant impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing a test system for multi-fuel, high-temperature fuel cells that can directly use carbon-based and anhydrous fuels while managing carbon deposition.
counterfactuals.output: A test system for evaluating multi-fuel, high-temperature fuel cells is disclosed. The system includes a thermally controlled test enclosure configured to receive at least one fuel-cell article, a configurable fuel-delivery assembly operable to supply carbon-containing fuels and substantially anhydrous fuels, and independently controlled oxidant and purge-gas circuits. The fuel-delivery assembly accommodates gaseous, liquid, and solid-derived fuels and includes heated conduits, metering devices, vaporizers, and optional fuel-conditioning modules. A control unit regulates cell temperature, pressure, fuel utilization, electrical loading, and gas composition to establish operating, carbon-deposition, and regeneration cycles. Carbon accumulation is detected or estimated using one or more of impedance, voltage, pressure-drop, mass-flow, gas-composition, optical, and temperature measurements. In response, the control unit modifies an operating parameter or introduces a controlled amount of steam, carbon dioxide, oxygen-containing gas, or electrochemically generated oxidant to inhibit, remove, or spatially control deposited carbon while maintaining fuel-cell operation. The enclosure may include removable electrodes, catalyst specimens, deposition collectors, and sampling ports for post-test characterization. The system thereby enables comparative testing of fuel-cell materials and architectures under direct-fuel conditions, including dry hydrocarbon, oxygenated, carbonaceous, and other anhydrous fuel feeds, while quantifying performance degradation, carbon tolerance, and regeneration effectiveness.

counterfactuals.output:
### Exemplary Patent Language

A multi-fuel solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) reactor comprising at least one electrochemical cell disposed between an anodic interconnection plate and a cathodic interconnection plate, the electrochemical cell including an electrolyte positioned between an anode and a cathode. The anodic interconnection plate defines at least one combustible-gas flow path configured to deliver a combustible gas to the anode, and the cathodic interconnection plate defines at least one oxidizing-gas flow path configured to deliver an oxidizing gas to the cathode, the combustible-gas flow path being fluidically isolated from the oxidizing-gas flow path during operation of the reactor.

The combustible gas may comprise hydrogen, a hydrocarbon, a carbonaceous synthesis gas, a gas produced by reforming a carbon-based fuel, or any combination thereof. Suitable carbon-based fuels include, without limitation, methane, natural gas, biogas, methanol, ethanol, gasoline, diesel fuel, kerosene, coal-derived fuel, biomass-derived fuel, and mixtures thereof. The reactor may be configured for internal reforming, external reforming, partial oxidation, gasification, or combinations thereof.

At least one component selected from the anode, cathode, electrolyte, anodic interconnection plate, cathodic interconnection plate, catalyst, and fuel-reforming medium may comprise one or more dopants. The one or more dopants may be present individually or collectively at a concentration greater than zero and up to about 20% by weight, based on the total weight of the doped component. The dopants may be selected to improve catalytic activity, ionic or electronic conductivity, resistance to carbon deposition, sulfur tolerance, thermal stability, mechanical integrity, or combinations thereof.

### Exemplary Independent Claim

1. A multi-fuel solid oxide fuel cell reactor, comprising:  
   an electrochemical cell comprising an anode, a cathode, and a solid oxide electrolyte disposed between the anode and the cathode;  
   an anodic interconnection plate adjacent to the anode and defining a combustible-gas flow path configured to convey a combustible gas comprising or derived from a carbon-based fuel across the anode; and  
   a cathodic interconnection plate adjacent to the cathode and defining an oxidizing-gas flow path configured to convey an oxidizing gas across the cathode,  
   wherein at least one of the anode, the cathode, the solid oxide electrolyte, the anodic interconnection plate, or the cathodic interconnection plate comprises at least one dopant at a concentration of up to 20% by weight of the component containing the dopant.
